walkthroughs.body_html:
Christians believeone God in three persons — the Trinity.

God is omnipotent (all-powerful), omniscient (all-knowing), omnibenevolent (all-loving), and just.

The Nicene Creed (325 CE) sets these out: 'We believe in one God, the Father almighty.'

Genesis 1-2: God created the universe in six days and rested on the seventh. Humans are made 'in the image of God'.

Incarnation: in Jesus, God became human. John 1:14 — 'The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.'

Christians celebrate the incarnation at Christmas.

Sin separates humans from God. Salvation repairs that.

Jesus' death (crucifixion) atones for sin; his resurrection brings eternal life.

Ephesians 2:8 — 'By grace you have been saved through faith.' Salvation is a free gift, received by trust in Jesus.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Christians believe in three different gods.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Jesus was half God and half human.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
